explanation: The positive pole is a retrospective detector of a word that reaches it as sub-word *pieces* rather than as one vocabulary token, and its gain is set by the surrounding text's language: it fires on bound fragments - word-initial (' ge' in Dutch geven, ' min' in minnow/minstrel/ministrant/' minzow', ' Magnet' in Magnetar, ' في' in بما في ذلك, ' ض' in ضعیف), medial ('elay' in melayani, 'ij' in vermijden, 'χ' in αρχικά, 'خ' in فخرا) and final ('ค' in คัพ, 'ی' in شناسایی, '{' in \frac{1}{2}) - reaching 3.3-7.8 inside Dutch sentences and 5.6-8.1 inside Persian/Thai text, but only 0.1-0.85 when the identical piece stands in German 'gegeben' or in English ('The geek', 'geven' quoted in an English sentence), and 0.0 where the same letters arrive as one whole token (' minimum' -0.1, ' mine' 0.0, ' mint' 0.1, against ' min'+'now' at 3.5-7.3). Because those bound pieces are ordinary in non-English web text, whole documents in Persian/Arabic script (5.5% of tokens active), Thai (3.2%), Korean (2.4%), Chinese (1.8%), Indonesian (5.7%) and Dutch web text (4.6%) fire throughout, while English prose sources stay silent (fineweb-edu 0.03%, c4 0.007%, wikitext 0.03%, pg19 0.008% of tokens): predict active when such a text contains a bound fragment token, and inactive for English/German/French prose and for text whose words are single vocabulary tokens.
